text:
Jordan Kim: morning folks, onboarding day 1. using fish on an M2 and my asdf shims aren't picked up by fish. installed asdf via brew. any fish-specific tips? :wave:
DevX Bot: welcome Jordan! paste `which python`, `echo $PATH` and `type -a asdf` in fish so we can see what's happening.
Jordan Kim: which python -> /usr/bin/python3, echo $PATH -> /usr/bin /usr/local/bin /opt/homebrew/bin /Users/jordan/.asdf/shims, type -a asdf -> asdf is a function
Maya: fish treats functions and PATH differently. add to ~/.config/fish/config.fish:
``
set -gx PATH /opt/homebrew/bin $HOME/.asdf/shims $PATH
status --is-interactive; and source (brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.fish
``
Carlos: note brew's asdf on some installs exposes asdf.fish instead of asdf.sh. also ensure `asdf reshim` after installs.
Jordan Kim: added that, restarted fish. `which python` -> /Users/jordan/.asdf/shims/python but `python --version` is 3.9. I need 3.11 (our repo uses 3.11).
Maya: run `asdf plugin-add python` if not already, then `asdf install python 3.11.4 && asdf global python 3.11.4 && asdf reshim`. if install fails, mac may need openssl/readline: `brew install openssl@3 readline` and set flags (fish uses set -x).
Jordan Kim: hit an SSL build error during install. brew suggested LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS. how do I translate those to fish? any quick snippet?
Carlos: in fish:
``
set -x LDFLAGS "-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib"
set -x CPPFLAGS "-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include"
```
Then re-run `asdf install`.
Jordan Kim: did that, python 3.11 installed. thanks! one more: our dotfiles use direnv (.envrc) to load secrets from 1password using the 1password CLI adapter. how do I get 1p CLI auth in fish? I use 1password.app with browser extension.
Maya: install 1password CLI (`brew install 1password-cli`) and run `eval (op signin --shorthand my)` in fish to set env. we usually do `set -x OP_SESSION_my (op signin --raw my)` so direnv can read it. you can add a helper function in ~/.config/fish/functions/op-login.fish for convenience.
OpsBot: FYI the onboarding script checks for OP_SESSION_* and will pause if not present. consider `op signin --raw <account>` in a terminal before running `./setup.sh`.
Jordan Kim: ran dotfiles setup, direnv denied .envrc because OP_SESSION missing. after signing in with op and `direnv allow` then `direnv export fish` it loaded vars and setup completed. all green.
Maya: pro tip for VS Code: either launch it from the terminal (`code .`) so it inherits fish env, or add the PATH lines to ~/.pam_environment on mac when starting from dock. also try the fish shell integration extension for better terminal behaviour.
Jordan Kim: huge help, thanks all! pinging @Maya if I hit any more snags. excited to be here :tada:
